t: A merchant republic on the lagoon, led by an elected doge and a closed hereditary nobility for about eleven centuries.
Its fleets and colonies, from Dalmatia to Crete and Cyprus, made it the main link between Latin Europe and the East.
Ottoman advances and new ocean routes eroded its power, and Napoleon ended the republic in 1797.
dyk: Venice opened the first public opera house, the Teatro San Cassiano, in 1637, when opera elsewhere was still largely a court entertainment.
ev: Traditional date of the election of Paolo Lucio Anafesto as first doge
Venetian merchants bring the relics of Saint Mark from Alexandria
Alexios I Komnenos grants Venice tax-free trade in the Byzantine Empire
The Fourth Crusade, led by Doge Enrico Dandolo, takes Constantinople
The Serrata closes the Great Council to a hereditary nobility
The Peace of Turin ends the War of Chioggia against Genoa
Cyprus falls to the Ottomans; the Holy League wins at Lepanto
Doge Ludovico Manin abdicates and the Great Council dissolves the republic

f.capital: Heraclea (Cittanova); Malamocco from 742; Venice (Rialto) from c. 811
